newsitem.title: UK: Moscow to hold Eurobond roadshow in May -dealers.
newsitem.headline: Moscow to hold Eurobond roadshow in May -dealers.

text.p: The City of Moscow plans to hold investor presentations to promote its debut Eurobond issue at the beginning of May, bankers said on Wednesday.
"Moscow's roadshow will take place in early May," a banker familiar with the transaction said.
Moscow is expected to issue a bond for up to $500 million. A three- or five-year maturity had been expected, but bankers said Moscow was likely to opt for the longer date.
"A five-year deal is expected," the banker said.
Credit Suisse First Boston and Nomura will together underwrite the bond.
Moscow's plans to raise money from the international bond markets were boosted when it was awarded high speculative grade credit ratings in February.

Its forthcoming Eurobond will be rated Ba2 by Moody's Investors Service and BB minus by Standard & Poor's, in line with Russia's rating. But both agencies said they were constrained by Russia's sovereign ceiling.
A number of other Russian borrowers are waiting to raise funds in the dollar bond market, including the city of St Petersburg, Nizhny Novgorod region and oil company LUKoil.
Russia itself tapped the Eurobond market for the first time since the 1917 revolution when it launched a $1.0 billion five-year bond last November.
Last month it issued a 2.0 billion mark seven-year bond, but so far no other Russian credit has come to the market.
